content: 1. Elexipag is a substrate of the ABCG2 (BCRP) transporter. When co-administered with ABCG2 (BCRP) inhibitors, monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects of selexipag. 2. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of sertraline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rolapitant may elevate plasma concentrations of CYP2D6 substrates for at least 28 days following administration. 3. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Oral rolapitant, as a P-gp inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates, potentially leading to adverse reactions. Monitor for adverse effects if concomitant use cannot be avoided. 4. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Plasma concentrations of CYP2D6 substrates may remain elevated for at least 28 days after rolapitant administration. 5. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Plasma concentrations of CYP2D6 substrates may remain elevated for at least 28 days after rolapitant administration. 6. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of rolapitant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of rolapitant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 8. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Do not exceed 18 mg per dose or 36 mg per day of deutetrabenazine in such cases. Monitor closely. 30.
